text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SREs + Eng-runtime — sudden quality regression alert on /v1/generate. Eval system spike: +6.4% failure rate (semantic drift). Trigger: routing change "billing-tier" rolled at 23:00 UTC.

maria: ack, oncall SRE here. Looking now.

jess: saw the alert, routing service deployed billing-tier map ~23:01. I'm on call for routing.

raj: i'm pulling router logs + recent rollout. quick grep shows mass hits to variant `gpt-econ-v0-quant` starting ~23:02.

leo: customers reporting more hallucinations in telemetry. Support seeing ~12 escalations in last 20m. @sophie can you confirm top affected customers?

sophie: yup quick list: org-12 (chatbot), org-77 (summarization). I'll open a customer-impact tracker and notif CS.

jess: can we confirm policy snippet that shipped? pasting from deploy:```yaml
routing_policy:
  - match: billing_tier == "free"
    route_to: gpt-econ-v0-quant
  - match: billing_tier == "standard"
    route_to: gpt-stable-v2
  - fallback: gpt-stable-v2
```

raj: that explains it — the policy maps free tier explicitly to an economy variant that hasn't passed our regression evals. Should have been shadow only.

maria: impact: increased quality alerts, some customers degraded but no backend error spikes. Latency unchanged. We should revert routing policy to previous behavior (shadow econ variant only).

jess: proposing immediate mitigation: set `billing_tier` mapping to `shadow` mode. Command: `redwoodctl routing update --policy billing-tier --set free:shadow`

raj: applying now. Running: `redwoodctl routing update --policy billing-tier --set free:shadow --reason "emergency rollback - quality regressions"`

raj: (logs) `2026-03-15T23:07:12Z routing-service PATCH policy billing-tier -> OK`

incident-bot: Deploy event: billing-tier policy updated by raj (rollback to shadow mode).

jess: good. I'm toggling the runtime override to prefer stable for existing in-flight sessions while the policy change propagates: `redwoodctl runtime override --set prefer_stable=true`

maria: monitoring eval-alerts and customer tickets. Initial numbers: quality alerts down from +6.4% to +1.2% in 3m.

sophie: pinged CS and informed top 5 customers; offering 2 hours of support credit and a brief postmortem.

leo: thanks. We need a postmortem and to prevent accidental promotion of economy variants. Assigning actions: lock routing policy deploys behind an additional QA gate and require explicit opt-in for economy variants.

jess: agreed. I'll create an RFC for gating and add an automated shadow-only flag for new variants. Also add a pre-deploy eval check that fails CI if eval regression > 1%.

maria: handing off to next oncall in 30m. Status: mitigation applied, alerts trending down, customer impact mitigated.

raj: note for postmortem — reason root cause was a human config change where `free` was set from `shadow` -> `active` during a policy YAML edit. We'll add lint to routing policy repo to catch `active` mapping to unverified variants.

eval-bot: regression alert cleared at 23:13 UTC. Rolling window back to baseline.

jess: summary for the pager — rolled back billing-tier map to shadow, runtime override prefer_stable applied, CS notified, postmortem owner jess, follow-up QA gating assigned.

maria: follow-up ops: capture traffic samples from 23:00-23:07 for replay in eval harness. raj can you export?

raj: exporting now: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-telemetry/streams/2026-03-15/23:00-23:10.gz ./`

sophie: closing immediate customer comms loop — CS will send template update and offer support.

jess: thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated with postmortem link when done. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) — Pager cleared at 23:20 UTC.
